- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 2024 (Feb–May), especially after sharp declines or spikes.
- Forecast shows gradual upward drift (e.g., +0.05–0.10 per day) while true prices often reverse or dip sharply, suggesting overconfidence in trend continuation.
- After price spikes (e.g., 70s–80s), model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections; forecasts remain elevated longer than actual.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates low prices and underestimates high prices, especially in mid-range zones (e.g., 60–70).
- Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days in downward trends; overestimates upward momentum in early periods.
- In May 2024, model fails to capture volatility spikes; forecasts remain flat while true prices surge or crash.
- Model assumes linear progression; true prices show non-linear corrections, especially after 60–70 thresholds.
- Overshoots after spikes (e.g., 80+ → 65+ forecast) and fails to adjust downward quickly; should cap forecasts at 10–15% below peak if spike >75.
- In low-price regimes (e.g., <60), model underestimates volatility and fails to anticipate sudden rebounds.
- Model does not account for seasonal or event-driven volatility; should adjust for calendar effects (e.g., end of quarter, policy announcements).
